analysis:
The change is documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md gains one table row at head line 1409 (outside the supplied excerpts), documenting a `decodeStepsBetweenPrefillChunks` scheduler setting (4 for the Qwen 3.5 family, else 0; `EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift`, `qwenDecodeStepsBetweenPrefillChunks`). The supplied head text (lines 1-805) is unchanged context. I examined it against the threat model for prefix-cache (T-041), TB-007 (inference engine) and TB-002.

The row describes a scheduling fairness knob: it interleaves decode-only steps after each prefill chunk. It does not touch encryption, attestation, authorization, key handling, cache scoping or cache-store behavior. The only residual security-relevant effect is a possible change in time-to-first-token and latency timing. That may marginally affect the already-accepted same-account TTFT oracle (SEC-035, T-041), but the supplied evidence shows no change to cache hit/miss semantics, so I do not treat it as a regression.

The source change that implements the setting is not in this batch, so I could not verify the claimed default values. The surrounding text on Super's SSD checkpoints is context only. It still matches T-041: encrypted under the provider cache root, scope-partitioned by authenticated tenant, and off without a scope. No new attack surface or invalidated assumption is shown. A follow-up pass should check that the Qwen decode-step default does not alter cache-publication or scope behavior.
